technical.lead: Zscaler ships first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI at Zenith Live
technical.body: At Zenith Live 2026 on June 9, Zscaler announced three products it positions as the industry's first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI: AI Broker enforces fine-grained access policies inline on MCP and A2A channels via an Agent Registry; AI Access Graph (built on the May 2026 $175 million Symmetry Systems acquisition) maps identity-to-data-source interconnections and enforces data-lineage policies in real time; and Endpoint AI Security extends threat detection to employee browsers, extensions, and locally installed AI tools. On June 10, Oasis Security announced an integration adding lifecycle governance for non-human identities on top of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange, delivering a unified control plane across machine-to-machine and agent-to-agent traffic.

technical.lead: Databricks launches Agent Bricks and OpenSharing to move agentic AI into production
technical.body: On June 16 at the Data + AI Summit, Databricks formally announced Agent Bricks, a three-pillar platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents at production scale. The Choice pillar covers frontier model access (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi) and a SpaceX partnership to serve Grok natively, with over 100,000 agents already built on the underlying infrastructure processing more than one quadrillion tokens annually. Context adds MCP integration with Unity Catalog for scoped access to Google Drive, JIRA, Slack, and GitHub, plus a Genie Ontology layer and an agent-memory service powered by Lakebase. Control delivers Unity AI Gateway for unified governance, contextual SQL security policies, and a Databricks Sandbox for isolated computing. Separately, Databricks and the Linux Foundation announced OpenSharing on June 10, an open vendor-neutral protocol extending Delta Sharing to agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data, with founding partners including OpenAI, SAP, Stripe, Atlassian, and Amadeus.

technical.lead: SGLang v0.5.13 promotes speculative decoding to production across FA3, MLA, and triton backends
technical.body: Released June 13, SGLang v0.5.13 adds model support for Nemotron 3 Ultra, Step-3.7-Flash, Command A+, and diffusion models including Cosmos 3, LingBot-World, SANA-WM, and FLUX.2-Klein. The release promotes Spec V2 tree drafting with topk greater than 1 to production-ready status across the triton, FA3, MLA, and aiter backends. Scheduler changes unify async value passing to reduce per-step overhead; DeepSeek V4 gains context parallelism, sparse-attention kernels, and MoE optimizations; SGLang-Diffusion adds real-time video generation with progressive resolution support. More than 70 developers contributed. SGLang already delivers roughly 29% higher throughput than vLLM on H100s (16,200 vs 12,500 tokens per second) and up to 6.4x gains on prefix-heavy workloads, and powers production deployments at xAI, Microsoft Azure, LinkedIn, and Cursor across approximately 400,000 GPUs.

technical.lead: Anthropic sends technical staff to Washington to negotiate Fable 5 export-control reversal
technical.body: Anthropic's dispute with the US government escalated on June 15 as the company dispatched senior technical staff to Washington to pursue a negotiated resolution following the June 12 directive suspending Fable 5 and Mythos 5. The administration cited a jailbreak technique; Anthropic's statement identifies the concern as asking the model to read a codebase and fix software flaws — standard defensive security work that security researcher Katie Moussouris noted on June 16 is precisely the most valuable task an AI can do for cyber defense, and that the same capability is present in competing systems including GPT-5.5. Negotiations are moving unusually fast, with at least some officials signaling openness to a technical compromise; as of June 16 both models remain offline globally. Anthropic stated that applying the same narrow-jailbreak-equals-recall standard industry-wide would effectively halt all new frontier model deployments.

technical.lead: Bay Area AI calendar fills: Data + AI Summit continues as security and chip events queue up
technical.body: The Databricks Data + AI Summit continues through June 18 at Moscone in San Francisco. Tonight, June 16, AICamp hosts an invite-only AI Agent Security Documentary Premiere (6-9 PM PDT, 582 Market St) featuring former White House CIO Theresa Payton and MIT's Ramesh Raskar. The Confidential Computing Summit runs June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation, confidential agents, 400-plus attendees). AI Tinkerers presents an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 with live agent attack surface demos. The AI Engineer World's Fair opens June 29-July 2 at Moscone West with dedicated Inference and Security tracks. AMD's Advancing AI 2026 lands July 23 at Moscone (Instinct/MI400-series focus). Hot Chips 2026 follows August 23-25 at Stanford; SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA's AI Summit runs August 1-6 in Las Vegas; and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 in Santa Clara.
